item.title: ‘The big advantage for us lies in flexibility’ – Electra manager Paul Tonini on battery storage
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Electra is increasingly relying on battery storage systems for its fast-charging parks. In Germany alone, 20 storage systems are already installed, and this number is expected to reach around 40 by the end of the year. In this interview, Germany CEO Paul Tonini explains the advantages of the technology, why grid operators sometimes complicate its deployment, and why battery storage alone cannot solve the challenges of expanding the charging network.

item.title: Fraunhofer explores lighter fuel cell bipolar plates
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: The Fraunhofer Institute for Machine Tools and Forming Technology (IWU) has developed new manufacturing processes for particularly lightweight bipolar plates made of carbon fiber-reinforced plastic. The technology could make fuel cells for drones, small aircraft, and helicopters lighter and more compact in the future.

item.title: Mercedes receives KBA approval for door-to-door driving assistant
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Mercedes-Benz has become the first automaker in Germany to receive regulatory approval for a point-to-point driving assistant. The German Federal Motor Transport Authority (KBA) approved the MB.Drive Assist Pro system based on UN Regulation R171. This enables automated door-to-door driving at SAE Level 2, including complex urban traffic situations.

item.title: Siemens introduces DC contactor for megawatt charging
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Siemens is expanding its DC portfolio with a high-performance DC contactor for voltages up to 1,500 volts and currents up to 600 amperes. The new SIRIUS 3QC1 combines semiconductor technology with mechanical contacts and is intended for use in megawatt charging stations for commercial vehicles.

item.title: Court deems BYD Ti7 too similar to JLR Defender
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: A Dutch court has ordered ten BYD subsidiaries in interim proceedings to refrain from building and selling the Ti7 in the EU. According to the judges, the model looks too similar to the JLR Defender. However, the main trial is still pending.

item.title: TruckCharge Network now integrates public chargers from Milence
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: Daimler Truck reports that its TruckCharge network now covers 21 markets and has recently integrated Milence's charging points. The initiative began in 2025 as a semi-public electric truck charging network with locations at dealers and customers. In addition to depot chargers, the integration of public chargers is also becoming increasingly important.

item.title: VW ID. Polo: customers now face year-long wait times
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Volkswagen has apparently significantly underestimated the success of its new electric small car family. Customers for the VW ID. Polo sometimes have to wait more than a year, and the other three models also require a lot of patience. Now, production in Spain is to be scaled up more quickly. However, a shortage of battery cells is also slowing down production.

item.title: Solaris delivers 13 hydrogen buses to France
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Solaris has delivered thirteen Urbino 12 hydrogen buses to the Béziers Méditerranée community association in southern France. In future, the vehicles will be used by the beeMob local transport network.

item.title: Adani Cement to deploy 410 heavy-duty electric trucks
item.dc:creator: Sagar Parikh
item.description: Indian cement manufacturer Adani Cement (Adani Group) has announced plans to add 410 heavy-duty electric trucks to its fleet. It has already flagged off the first batch as part of the initiative and will commission the remaining trucks by March 2027.

item.title: EU Council signals shift away from binding EV quotas for corporate fleets
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: When presenting the 'Auto Package', the EU Commission included a draft passage requiring member states to set concrete mandates for the ramp-up of electric company cars from 2030. However, the EU Parliament then downgraded the proposed binding quotas to voluntary targets - and the Council now seems to be following suit.

item.title: Aachen startup Cylib acquires BASF’s battery recycling business
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: In a major development for what is a relatively young company, Aachen-based battery recycling startup Cylib is taking over BASF's mucbh battery recycling business. The deal includes, among other things, two facilities in Schwarzheide (Brandenburg) and the North America business.

item.title: EU and Indonesia agree free trade deal to cut tariffs on cars
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: The EU and Indonesia have signed a far-reaching free trade agreement and an investment protection agreement. Under the deal, Indonesian import tariffs on European cars, which currently reach up to 50 per cent, are to be phased out over the next five years. The EU also expects to gain better access to key raw materials.

item.title: Opel and Leapmotor formalise battery-electric SUV partnership
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Opel and Leapmotor have officially agreed to collaborate on the development of a new electric SUV. With a launch date penned for 2028, the model will use key components from the Chinese manufacturer and will be produced at Stellantis' plant in Zaragoza, Spain.

item.title: EU-China hybrid import quota unlikely to apply to range extenders
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: The annual import quota of 350,000 hybrid vehicles agreed upon between the EU and China in October apparently does not include electric vehicles with range extenders. Instead, these cars are likely to continue being classified as battery-electric vehicles and thus be subject to the special tariffs on EVs, but no import quota would apply.

item.title: BMW iX4 rolls off production line alongside iX3 in Debrecen
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: Following the BMW iX3, series production of the BMW iX4 has now also begun at BMW's plant in Debrecen - making the new SUV, with its coupé silhouette, the second model of the Neue Klasse to be produced at the Hungarian BMW plant. The iX4 will reach dealers starting March 2027 - initially in two drivetrain variants.

item.title: Chinese electric SC01 sportscar to be built in Italy from May 2027
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: The company FIPA plans to establish a new production site for EVs in the Marken region of eastern Italy. From the end of May 2027, a Chinese electric sports car - the SC01 - will be assembled there. By 2030, the company aims to employ 285 people and later expand production to include light electric vehicles.

item.title: Lagos further expands electric bus fleet
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Eleven new electric buses for public transport have been introduced in Lagos, Nigeria. The vehicles are from Oando Clean Energy and represent the first batch of a planned delivery of 50 electric buses. In the long term, 552 e-buses are to be deployed on the routes across the megacity.

item.title: VW to present battery-electric VW ID. Polo GTI concept – for the racetrack
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: A 240 km/h top speed and 0 to 100 km/h in 4.7 seconds: with the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept, Volkswagen is demonstrating how the GTI idea can evolve in the electric age. The sprint-strong study delivers 270 kW - that's nearly 370 hp in old currency.

item.title: GTA VI fans praise lightning-fast EV charging speeds
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: The hype around Grand Theft Auto VI is enormous - and the automotive industry is getting heavily involved. BMW, Daimler Truck, and Sixt are using the game’s aesthetic for their social media presence. But electromobility also has its place in the game itself: in Vice City, charging EVs happens much faster than in real life.

item.title: ESB and Tesco Ireland plot 200 kW EV chargers at five stores
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: ESB and Tesco Ireland have agreed a new partnership to expand public EV charging at Tesco stores across the country. The first phase will see fast and ultra-fast chargers rated up to 200 kW installed at five Tesco sites in Clarehall, Clearwater, Drogheda, Dundalk and Maynooth.

item.title: Renault Twingo E-Tech: UK pricing revealed
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: Renault has confirmed UK pricing for the new all-electric Twingo E-Tech, with the small city car starting at £14,745 once the full £3,750 Electric Car Grant (ECG) is applied. Orders will open in the first quarter of 2027, with customer deliveries expected by March.

item.title: India: Energy In Motion secures order for 500 electric heavy-duty trucks
item.dc:creator: Sagar Parikh
item.description: Indian electric trucking solutions provider Energy In Motion (EIM), an associate company of Ravindra Energy, has bagged a major order for 500 heavy-duty trucks from Sorigin Green Mobility, a homegrown electric truck fleet operator. The duo have signed a memorandum of understanding to deploy these trucks over a period of two years.

item.title: Zenobē expands into Germany
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: British commercial fleet electrification specialist Zenobē is bringing its offerings to Germany. Zenobē provides fleet operators with a fixed-price solution that includes EVs, charging infrastructure, battery management, and fleet management software.

item.title: Aptera completes first customer vehicle
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: California-based solar electric vehicle developer Aptera has completed its first vehicle destined for a customer. The three-wheeled solar car is set to be delivered to an early investor outside the US.

item.title: Volkswagen ID. Cross opens for UK orders from £26,985
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: Volkswagen has opened UK order books for its new all-electric ID. Cross, with prices starting at £26,985. However, entry-level versions will not be available to order until January 2027, meaning customers currently have a choice of two models with the larger battery.

item.title: Onsemi introduces new SiC Platform: EliteSiC M4
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: US semiconductor manufacturer Onsemi has introduced the fourth generation of its silicon carbide technology with EliteSiC M4. The new platform is set to increase power density by up to 30 per cent and reduce losses by up to 35 per cent. This could benefit, among other things, the drivetrain systems of electric vehicles.

item.title: Ford Trucks partners with Circulor for battery passport
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Ford is working with technology company Circulor to prepare the its electric truck batteries for the requirements of the European Battery Passport. The focus is on the traceability of battery materials and the collection of supply chain data.

item.title: Hongqi EHS4: a battery-electric SUV with Leapmotor technology for Europe
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Chinese automaker Hongqi is introducing a new eSUV to Europe. The FAW-owned brand will first launch the EHS4 in Italy with a base starting price of €35,900. However, this will be lowered to €32,900 during an initial promotional period.

item.title: Alpitronic builds DC fast charger factory in South Carolina, USA
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: Alpitronic is expanding its presence in the USA and investing nearly US$34 million in its own production facility for fast-charging stations in South Carolina. Additionally, the South Tyrolean charging infrastructure specialist is strengthening its North America management with Christopher Balcom as the new Chief Commercial Officer.

item.title: ‘Nova’: Moment Energy launches second-life battery storage system
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: Canadian battery technology firm Moment Energy has unveiled Nova, a new battery energy storage system (BESS) built using repurposed EV batteries. The system is now in production at the company's Megafactory 1, with orders open and initial deliveries planned for Q1 2027.
